prompt: can you see if readme file is all upto date.

tasks.title: Audit README against current CLI and workflow
tasks.spec: Review README.md against the current implementation and update it so every user-facing claim matches the code. Use agenthub/cli.py as the source of truth for commands and flags, agenthub/config.py for config keys and defaults, agenthub/models.py plus agenthub/progress.py for task statuses and runtime phases, agenthub/researcher.py and agenthub/validator.py for the research and validation phases, agenthub/notifier.py for notification behavior, and agenthub/state.py for log artifacts. In README.md, fix stale defaults such as `branch_prefix`, document the full command surface (`--prompt-file` and `-f`, stdin `-`, `status`, `log`, `resume`, `retry`, `clean`, `clean --logs`, and `config`), update prerequisites to mention installed `claude` or `codex` CLIs as valid backends in addition to API keys, refresh the workflow description to include complexity gating, optional research, scheduling, validation, rollback and safe-branch behavior on validation failure, and cleanup semantics, replace the outdated reviewer description with the current 8-check review model, expand the configuration section to cover all current keys and defaults, and refresh the logs section to reflect `plan.json`, `research.json`, `validation-*.json`, task round logs, and `summary.md`. Keep the README concise and user-facing, and do not change runtime code.
tasks.rationale: This is a single documentation-maintenance change centered on README.md. The README is materially stale in several concrete places: it documents `branch_prefix: tmp/af` even though agenthub/config.py defaults to `tmp/ah`; it omits user-facing commands implemented in agenthub/cli.py such as `clean` and the `--logs` cleanup mode; it frames prerequisites as API-key-only even though `check_api_keys()` accepts installed `claude` and `codex` CLIs; it describes review as a narrow spec-compliance check even though agenthub/models.py and the reviewer prompts now enforce an 8-check rubric; and it does not explain the current research and validation phases or the newer config surface added for them. Leaving these mismatches in place will mislead users about how to run, configure, and trust the tool. A single senior engineer can audit and refresh this file in one sitting, so splitting it would add coordination overhead without improving quality.
